title: Heat Pump Rebates in Glendale 2026: Up to $5,000 from GWP | HomePowerRebate
desc: Glendale Water and Power pays $1,000 per ton, up to $5,000, when a heat pump replaces a gas furnace or gas and electric HVAC. Ratings, permits, limits and steps.
lead: Glendale Water and Power pays $1,000 for every ton of heat pump that replaces a gas furnace or a gas and electric system, up to $5,000. That is one of the largest heat pump rebates in the Los Angeles area, and the paperwork is where most of the effort goes.
cards_heading: What Glendale Water and Power pays
cards_intro: These figures come from the Home Energy and Water Saving Rebates page of Glendale Water and Power (GWP), which we read on October 2, 2026. GWP says its updated amounts took effect November 1, 2025, and that funds are first come, first served. You must be a GWP customer, and the unit must be installed at a home GWP serves.

cards.title: Replacing gas heating (or gas and electric HVAC)
cards.note: Up to $5,000, paid as a check. Needs a finalized Building and Safety mechanical permit.

cards.title: Replacing an existing heat pump
cards.note: Up to $2,500, paid as a bill credit.

cards.title: Panel upgrade with a heat pump
cards.note: Only when paired with a heat pump or heat pump water heater. Needs a finalized electrical permit. Paid as a check.

cards.title: Efficiency minimums
cards.note: Plus ENERGY STAR and an AHRI certificate for the system.

after_cards:
What that looks like in dollars

A 3-ton system that replaces a gas furnace earns 3 x $1,000 = $3,000. A 5-ton system reaches the $5,000 cap. If the same job also needs a panel upgrade, add $1,000. Swapping one heat pump for a newer one pays 3 x $500 = $1,500 for 3 tons, as a bill credit, not a check. The second figure is much lower, so the difference between replacing gas and replacing a heat pump is worth confirming with your installer before you quote.
sections: What GWP checks before it pays

The ratings come first. The system needs at least 15.2 SEER2 and 7.8 HSPF2, ENERGY STAR status, and an AHRI certificate that your installer can get for you. GWP allows one rebate per story every 10 years for a ducted or packaged unit and one per room every 10 years for a ductless mini-split. A home with two stories and a separate studio can use the allowance more than once, which is the practical difference between ducted and ductless here.

GWP also says rebates are not guaranteed until it verifies them, and that a rebate cannot exceed the purchase price. Ask your installer to write the tonnage and the AHRI number on the invoice so there is no question later.

The $1,000 per ton amount needs a finalized Building and Safety mechanical permit. Glendale takes permits through its online Glendale Permits portal, and inspections are requested there after you log in. The City's permit services page lists the Permit Services Center at (818) 548-3200 for questions. The City adopted a new fee schedule on June 23, 2026, and some fees took effect July 1, so ask your installer for the current permit cost instead of an old quote.

A permit is not a formality for the rebate. If it is not finalized, GWP does not pay the larger amount. Ask your installer to schedule the inspection and to tell you when it passes.
Your utility: Glendale Water and Power

GWP is the City's own utility, and it sets these amounts itself. That is why Glendale pays several times what Pasadena does per ton (Pasadena pays $170, see Pasadena heat pump rebates) and more than Burbank, which caps its rebate at $2,500. If GWP serves your address you are in a good spot. GWP's customer service line on its rebate page is 855-550-4497.

The panel rebate matters too. Homes in older neighborhoods may need a bigger panel before a heat pump fits, and GWP is the only utility in this part of Los Angeles County whose page lists a panel rebate we could verify.

Glendale's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 8.1°C (about 47°F), and the coldest recorded day in that stretch was -0.1°C. That is mild enough that any heat pump meeting GWP's ratings will do the job, so you do not need to pay extra for a cold-climate model. Where money is lost is in oversizing. A unit that is too large costs more, short-cycles and earns the same rebate per ton only up to the cap. Ask your installer how they sized it, and ask for a load calculation, not a rule of thumb.

The federal 25C tax credit ended for spending after December 31, 2025. Statewide heat pump help from TECH Clean California and the federal HEEHRA program is fully reserved and takes new requests on hold only. The Switch Is On California site lists more incentives you may qualify for, but GWP's rebate is the main one that is open for Glendale homes today.
installers_intro: These Glendale heat pump and HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone. Ask each for the tonnage, the SEER2 and HSPF2 numbers, the AHRI certificate and who schedules the permit inspection.
claim_heading: How to claim the GWP rebate
claim_steps: Check that GWP is your electric utility, and that the system will be installed at a GWP-served home.
Choose a heat pump rated at least 15.2 SEER2 and 7.8 HSPF2, and ask for the AHRI certificate.
Have your installer pull the Building and Safety mechanical permit and get it finalized by inspection.
Apply on the GWP rebate page within 12 months of the purchase date, with the invoice, AHRI certificate and permit.
Add the panel upgrade rebate if the job includes one, with its electrical permit.
Wait for GWP to verify. The larger rebate arrives as a check and the smaller one as a bill credit.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in Glendale?
$1,000 per ton, up to $5,000, when a heat pump replaces a gas furnace or a gas and electric HVAC system. Replacing an existing heat pump pays $500 per ton, up to $2,500.
Is the rebate a check or a bill credit?
The $1,000 per ton rebate is a check. The $500 per ton rebate for replacing a heat pump is a bill credit.
How long do I have to apply?
GWP says applications must be submitted no more than 12 months from the date of purchase.
Yes. The larger rebate needs a finalized Building and Safety mechanical permit, and a panel upgrade needs its own finalized electrical permit.
Can I get a rebate for each room with a mini-split?
GWP allows one rebate per room every 10 years for a ductless mini-split and one per story for ducted or packaged systems.
Is the $1,000 per ton amount permanent?
GWP calls the increased amounts limited and says funds are first come, first served. Confirm before you buy.
